title: Files That Follow You
tagline: Build your real cloud vault — done before Lesson 2.
objectives: I can build my real folder system in Google Drive and find it from any device.
I know OneDrive and Google Drive are two separate cloud stores, and which kind of work lives in each.
I can create, save and re-open a file in the cloud.

config.headline: Files that follow you.
lines: In Mission Control you filed pretend files into a pretend Vault.
This side quest is the real thing: you'll build your actual folders, in your actual clouds — and the website will check your Google Drive ones are really there.
Twenty minutes, any device, any time — but have it done before Lesson 2.
Two clouds — and both of them yours. Let's set them up.
config.help: This screen is only for reading — it tells you what today's lesson is about. When the writing finishes, press the button at the bottom to start.

config.intro: Google Drive is the cloud that follows your C2k login to ANY device — school, home, even a phone. Time to build your Vault in it, for real.

steps.title: Open your real Drive
steps.text: Log into My-School, the way you do every day. In the Launch panel, click View All, then Google Workspace, then Launch App under Google Drive. If Google Drive is already a tile in your Launch panel, click that instead. At home you can go straight to drive.google.com and sign in with your C2k email (yourusername@c2ken.net).

clip.label: Show me how
clip.title: Getting into Drive and building your folders
clip.note: The film does this whole card: getting into Drive, building School, building DT Work inside it, and putting a first document in. The one it makes is called Test Document - yours gets your codename instead.

captions.text: Click 'View All' from the Launch section
Click 'Google Workspace', then launch the Google Drive app (if the app is already on the Launch section, click it from there instead.)
Click on 'New', 'New Folder', and name it 'School'. Then click 'Create'
We'll put a folder inside our 'School' folder by double-clicking on it.
Follow the same steps as before to create a new folder, and name it 'DT Work'
We'll create a new document that will live inside the DT Work folder. Click New, Google Docs, then Blank Document

Give the document a name. Documents created within Google Drive are automatically saved any time you add something or make a change - just look for the little tick inside the cloud and you'll know it is saved

You can see that the document lives inside the DT Work folder, which lives inside the School folder, which lives inside My Drive. Subfolders are folders that live inside other folders - so DT Work is a subfolder inside School.

steps.title: Create your School folder
steps.text: Click + New (top-left) → New folder. Name it exactly: School — capital S, nothing else. This is the top of your filing system, just like the Vault.

steps.title: Create DT Work inside School
steps.text: Open your School folder (double-click it), then + New → New folder again. Name this one exactly: DT Work. This is your DT home on the Google side. Work you make with Google's tools lives here, and so do the files your DT lessons ask you to save. Your DT teacher can find it when you share it.

steps.title: Put your first real file in it
steps.text: Inside DT Work, click + New, then Google Docs, then Blank document. A blank document opens - type your codename (or your name, if Lesson 1 hasn't given you a codename yet), then close the tab. No save button needed: Google Docs saves to the cloud as you type.
steps.confirm: My first file is in DT Work

steps.title: Prove the cloud kept it
steps.text: Close the Doc's tab, then open drive.google.com fresh and double-click your file inside DT Work. Your words are still there — nothing was ever "saved" by you, and nothing was lost. That is the whole point of the cloud.
steps.confirm: I re-opened my file and my words were there

config.help: Work through the steps in order in a second tab — this tab is your checklist. Names matter: School and DT Work, spelled exactly, capitals and all — the inspection checks the real names.

config.checking: Looking inside your real Drive for your folders…
config.errorText: The website could not be reached just then. Nothing is lost — try again in a moment.
config.intro: Now prove it. The website will look inside your actual Google Drive — with your permission, that is what the tick-boxes on your first day allowed — and check the folders are really there. Nothing else is looked at: just the two folder names.

checks.label: A folder named School in My Drive
A folder named DT Work inside School

config.passText: Inspection PASSED. Your Vault is real, and it will follow you to every device you ever sign in on. That has earned you the Vault Builder badge — 20 XP. Press the button below to claim it, and the points are banked.
config.failText: Not there yet — that's fixable in under a minute. Check the exact names and try the inspection again.
config.help: Press the button and the website checks your real Drive for the two folders. If it fails, the message names what's missing — fix it in the Drive tab and run it again. You can retry as often as you like.

config.intro: Here's the twist: your C2k login comes with TWO clouds. OneDrive is Microsoft's — it's where Word, Excel and PowerPoint work lives, in DT and in lots of your other subjects. Same idea as Drive, different building.

steps.title: Open your OneDrive
steps.text: Log into My-School, the way you do every day. In the Launch panel, click Microsoft 365 Web Apps. When it opens, click the squares menu in the very top-left corner and choose OneDrive - if you cannot see it there, type OneDrive into the search box at the top of that menu. Then click My files, down the left-hand side.

clip.label: Show me how
clip.title: Getting into OneDrive and building your folders
clip.note: That squares menu sits in the very top-left corner of every Microsoft 365 page. The film goes on to make a Word document inside DT Work - you do not have to do that part, it is showing you what this cloud is for.

captions.text: Click 'Microsoft 365' from the Launch section
Click the grid of dots on the top left
Click on 'OneDrive'. You can search for it if you can't see it
Click 'My Files'
Click 'Create or Upload', then 'Folder'
Choose a colour for your folder if you'd like, name it 'School', then click 'Create'
We'll put a folder inside our 'School' folder by clicking on it.
Follow the same steps as before to create a new folder, and name it 'DT Work'
You can see that this DT Work folder lives inside the School folder, which lives inside My Files. Subfolders are folders that live inside other folders - so DT Work is a subfolder inside School.
We'll create a Word document that will be saved in the DT Work folder
Inside the DT Work folder, click 'Create or Upload'. You'll see a range of Microsoft products that you can create and save there. Click Word Document.
Give it a name, and watch how it saves automatically (the green tick inside the cloud)
You can see that, because we created the document inside the folder we wanted it to live in, that's where we will find it.

steps.title: Build a School folder here too
steps.text: Click + Create or upload, then Folder. Name it exactly: School - you can pick a folder colour too, if you like. Now both of your clouds have the same tidy top level - future-you will be very grateful.

steps.title: And DT Work inside it
steps.text: Open your School folder, then click + Create or upload and Folder again, and name it exactly: DT Work. Now BOTH of your clouds have the same two folders. This one is your DT home on the Microsoft side - later in the course, the DT work you make in Word, Excel or PowerPoint will live here.
steps.confirm: DT Work is inside School — in OneDrive too

steps.title: Know which cloud a file lives in
steps.text: The app you made a file in tells you which cloud it lives in. Work made in Word, Excel or PowerPoint → OneDrive. Work made in Google Docs → Google Drive. They are two SEPARATE places — a file saved in one is not in the other. In DT you will use BOTH, and every lesson tells you which one, so you never have to guess.
steps.confirm: I know how to tell which cloud a file lives in

config.help: Follow the route exactly: My-School → Launch → Microsoft 365 Web Apps → the squares menu → OneDrive. If a sign-in appears at home, it is the normal school one.

config.intro: One scenario before the side quest closes.

items.stem: You typed an essay in Word Online for English, and made a quiz in Google Docs for DT. Which is TRUE?
options: The essay is in OneDrive and the quiz is in Google Drive — two separate clouds
Both files are in the same place, because it's the same login
The files copy themselves between the two clouds overnight
Neither is saved unless you clicked a save button

config.help: One marked question. Your verdict arrives when the report files.

statements: I can open my Google Drive from any device.
I built my School and DT Work folders for real.
I know OneDrive and Google Drive are two different clouds.
